**Published online:**
Sep 1, 2026

**Geographic focus:**
Asia (Japan), North America (USA) — bilateral monetary policy coordination

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — references prior BOJ hikes, July 31 joint intervention, June rate hike to 1%
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting, near-term rate hike expectations, yen volatility
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — quarterly hike trajectory, inflation overshoot risk, ongoing tightening cycle

**Synopsis:**
US Treasury Secretary Bessent met BOJ Governor Ueda at the G20 in Asheville, explicitly backing decisive BOJ monetary tightening to address yen undervaluation and domestic Japanese inflation. The US effectively pressured the BOJ to hike at its Sep 17-18 meeting. Markets have near-fully priced a September hike. The article signals a potential shift toward a quarterly BOJ tightening pace, up from the current ~twice-per-year cadence. The US and Japan previously conducted a rare joint yen-buying intervention on Jul 31, though its effect proved temporary.
